top_story: The mining of commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz escalated sharply by 14 November, with three tankers set ablaze after striking mines, deepening a pattern that has already killed 25 seafarers since the US-Israel war on Iran began. This marks a shift from strategic pressure on states to direct danger for civilian crews and global energy transit, raising the cost of insecurity for Gulf societies and international markets alike. In Gaza, the 12 November strike on Nasser hospital in Khan Younis killed a surgeon and five others at one of the territory’s last functioning medical sites, and the following day a baby died of hypothermia as attacks and aid restrictions compounded the collapse of civilian protection. Taken together, the latest developments show a regional war increasingly defined by attritional harm to civilians and essential infrastructure, with the human toll now reinforcing the conflict’s wider economic and political destabilization.
